engine.meaning: Nearly all of it is the original verbatim, so the points survive, but "Pages knocks together out draft updates to your site" garbles the preview point and "knock together" implies a rough job.
engine.sense: "knock together" (make hastily and roughly) is used for "builds" in "Pages knocks together out draft updates" and "used to knock together many different types of sites", a wrong connotation for a product pitch; "flamin' easy" strains in official copy.
engine.authenticity: Mechanical: "It’s flamin' easy to host static website files on Pages" sits in otherwise untouched US government prose; "customizable" kept.
engine.register: Essentially untranslated: "The hardest part is often not crafting the content or designing the website". Only "knocks together", "flamin'" and "organisation" change.
engine.tone: The upbeat, promotional tone survives as the text is unchanged, though "flamin' easy" jars.
engine.flow: "Pages knocks together out draft updates to your site at a special preview URL" is ungrammatical.

unharnessed.meaning: All points kept: the compliance burden, Pages' role, FedRAMP, previews and sign-off, and the four static-site advantages ("where you only pay for what you use").
unharnessed.sense: Most terms fit ("compliance grunt work", "fewer weak spots", "knock up a website"), but "it's easy to get the tick-off on content updates from stakeholders" says "tick-off", which in Australia is a reprimand ("a ticking-off"), not approval.
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural ("Static websites have a few things going for them", "Steering clear of a traditional CMS means steering clear of headaches"); "knock up a website" may raise a smirk.
unharnessed.register: A steady level 3 that keeps the official headings and technical terms intact. No swearing.
unharnessed.tone: Upbeat and promotional, as the original.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "That means the whole website's easier to look after and has fewer weak spots."
unharnessed.variety: Good range, with "steering clear" doubled deliberately and "sites" repetition in places.

dinkum-3.meaning: All points kept, reworded faithfully ("A production-level static site generally needs one simple static file server or service, not dozens."); "and we know what we're doing" renders "expertly".
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "the hard yakka usually isn't writing the content", "is no drama", "have a fair bit going for them", "without any fuss".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural, with "hard yakka" a slightly stock choice; "Fully customisable" spelt the Australian way.
dinkum-3.register: Right at level 3, keeping the technical content clear. No swearing.
dinkum-3.tone: Upbeat and confident, as the original.
dinkum-3.flow: Reads naturally: "Skip the traditional CMS and you skip the headaches that come with it".
dinkum-3.variety: Varied: "hard yakka", "sorted", "no drama", "a fair bit going for them", "without any fuss".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: All points kept ("and it's easy to get the tick from stakeholders on content updates"); "and doing it properly" renders "expertly".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "get the tick from stakeholders", "fewer weak spots", "compliance sorted".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Natural; "Fair go, it shouldn’t be like that." is a slightly forced use of "fair go" as an opener.
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 3, no swearing; technical terms preserved.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth, but "looking after" repeats ("looking after server applications", "easier to look after"), and "You can build all sorts of sites with static sites" is clunky.
yarn-dinkum.variety: Good range, with "look after" used three times ("Pages looks after", "looking after server applications", "easier to look after").

yarn-troppo.meaning: All points kept, but colour adds claims: "when they're already flat out" (the original only says extra strain), "you only pay for what you use, not a cent more", "Easy, you reckon."
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly fits ("a whole swag of headaches", "get the nod from stakeholders", "keep it ticking over"), though "fewer holes for the baddies to poke at" stretches "fewer vulnerabilities" into a jokey picture.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Many natural lines, but forced ones too: "and doing it like it knows what it's on about", "Translation:", "no two ways about it".
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3, nearer a yarn: "odds are someone's dropped what sounds like a dead simple job on your desk", "comes piling through the door". No swearing.
yarn-troppo.tone: Still upbeat and promotional, though the jokes ("the baddies") make a government page sound flippant in places.
yarn-troppo.flow: Piles up: "taking care of the backend and compliance grind for launching and running a website, and doing it like it knows what it's on about, so you can put your know-how where it counts: your content."
yarn-troppo.variety: Very varied: "hard yakka", "squared away", "flat out", "swag", "nursing", "easy as", "get the nod".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the Pages pitch, though recast as a sales yarn.

engine.why: Broken grammar, and "knock together" suggests slapdash work in a product pitch.

unharnessed.original: get signoff on content updates from stakeholders

"knock up" also means to get someone pregnant; a risky choice in work copy.

dinkum-3.quote: Pages is there for our fellow federal partners: we handle the backend

summaries.engine: A word-swap pass with a wrong-connotation "knock together" and broken grammar; otherwise untranslated.
summaries.unharnessed: Faithful and natural at level 3, but "tick-off" takes the opposite sense.
summaries.dinkum-3: The most even: faithful, natural, varied and right at level 3.
summaries.yarn-dinkum: Faithful and natural at the right weight; a little repetitive.
summaries.yarn-troppo: Lively and varied but heavier than level 3, with added claims and some forced lines.
